Editor-in-Chief, Infectio. https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5410-5997 4 Universidad de Córdoba, Facultad Ciencias de la Salud, Departamen- to de Regencia en Farmacia, Monteria Córdoba, Colombia. https://orcid. org/0000-0001-5616-1071 Recibido: 25/08/2026; Aceptado: 25/08/2026 Cómo citar este artículo: S. Mattar, et al. Hantavirus: From Seoul to the Andes — The Imperative Need to Include It in the Triage of Acute Febrile Syndrome. Infectio 2026; 30(3): 245-246 Keywords: Hantavirus, Acute Febrile Syndrome, Rattus norvegicus Palabras clave: Hantavirus, Síndrome febril agudo, Rattus norvegicus Hantaviruses belong to two worlds: the Old-World Seoul vi- rus (SV) and New World hantaviruses, such as the Sin Nombre virus (SNV) in North America and Andes virus in South Ameri- ca. SV is a cosmopolitan hantavirus that is transmitted by the common brown rat (Rattus norvegicus). The virus lives in urban rodents and travels on ships. It causes hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), which has low lethality. New World hantaviruses, such as SNV and Andes virus, cause Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome (HCPS), a condition with high lethality ranging between 30% and 40%. The transmission routes for both groups are similar, primarily occurring through contact with aerosolized rodent excretions and secretions1. The geography of zoonotic diseases is often marked by pro- found contrast. In the fabric of global health, few pathogens exemplify this as starkly as hantavirus. In the Old World, SV adapted to synanthropic rodents (Rattus rattus, Rattus nor- vegicus, and Mus musculus), which in turn adapted to urban environments enriched with human food waste. SV is trans- mitted in metropolitan settings with moderate lethality ra- tes, although it may be underdiagnosed or misdiagnosed as other conditions, such as leptospirosis, particularly in Latin America, where cases are rarely reported2. In contrast, the na- rrative of the New World SNV changes completely. * Autor para correspondencia: Correo electrónico: smattar@correo.unicordoba.edu.co; mattarsalim@gmail.com In the Americas, hantaviruses emerge from wild ecosystems with high virulence and present clinically as HCPS. The vec- tors of these viruses are wild sigmodontine rodents (Oligory- zomys, Proechimys, Peromyscus, and Calomys) that feed on crops and local flora. However, evidence has demonstrated that SNV can infect multiple rodent species within geogra- phic regions experiencing human cases. This suggests that several rodent species may act as reservoirs and potential vectors for the transmission of H. longicornis to humans. Re- servoirs identified by SNV include Peromyscus boylii, Tamias minimus, and Mus musculus. The latter is ubiquitous in hou- seholds worldwide and is a well-known vector of the lym- phocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) and Leptospira (3). New World hantaviruses are widely distributed across North America and exhibit high diversity, including SNV, New York virus, and Black Creek Canal virus in the United States; Cho- clo virus in Panama; Maporal virus in Venezuela; Machupo virus in Bolivia; Laguna Negra virus in Paraguay; Sabiá virus in Brazil; and the recently prominent Andes virus (ANDV) in Argentina and Chile (Figure 1). Following the corridor of the formidable Andes mountain range, the virus moves steadily alongside its rodent hosts across the mountains, jungles, and valleys. ANDV has cha- llenged the classical virological paradigm that orthohanta- viruses are transmitted strictly via exposure to rodent secre- tions and excretions. ANDV possesses the unique capacity S. Mattar, et al 246 ASOCIACIÓN COLOMBIANA DE INFECTOLOGÍA REVISTA INFECTIO for interhuman airborne transmission, as documented during the M/V Hondius cruise ship outbreak in April 2026. A total of 13 confirmed cases and three fatalities were epidemio- logically linked to the vessel, forcing numerous passengers into mandatory quarantine across various countries. Never- theless, person-to-person transmission remains uncommon and is predominantly associated with household exposure, intimate contact, caregiving without adequate personal pro- tective equipment, and prolonged exposure to poorly venti- lated or overcrowded environments4,5. This epidemiological journey, spanning from the alleys of Seoul to the forested regions of South America, is not a ran- dom evolutionary artifact but rather a direct reflection of environmental boundaries repeatedly breached by human activity. Today, hantaviruses are no longer exotic rarities con- fined to the pages of tropical medicine textbooks. Accele- rating ecological degradation and expanding anthropogenic frontiers force host reservoirs out of mountain ranges and wild savannas into closer proximity to human populations. The evolving landscape of hantavirus infections poses a ma- jor diagnostic and therapeutic challenge for infectious disea- se specialists. The core challenge lies not merely in managing critical clinical outcomes but in establishing early clinical sus- picion. The eco-epidemiology of the disease demands the inclusion of hantavirus in diagnostic algorithms for acute undifferentiated febrile illness in emergency departments. Early symptoms overlap with numerous seasonal and tropical pathogens; thus, the differential diagnosis must encompass influenza, betacoronavirus infections, mycoplasmosis, Q fe- ver, leptospirosis, malaria, rickettsiosis, dengue, Zika, Chikun- gunya, Mayaro, and Oropouche5. Importantly, preceding the ANDV outbreak on the M/V Hon- dius in April 2026, the Ministry of Public Health of Argentina confirmed 12 hantavirus cases and two deaths in Salta Pro- vince between January and March. Most infections occurred in the Orán Department, involving 10 men and two women aged 20–50 years, while 50 additional suspected cases remai- ned under investigation across multiple departments6. Similarly, between February and July 2026, the Ministry of Health of Chile confirmed 41 hantavirus cases and 14 deaths (34% mortality rate). Cases were reported across 11 regions from Valparaíso to Aysén, with the highest incidence rates per 100,000 inhabitants recorded in Aysén (1.84), Los Ríos (0.96), and Ñuble (0.95). The causative agent was identified as ANDV, vectored by the long-tailed pygmy rice rat (Oligoryzomys lon- gicaudatus). In Venezuela, by late July 2026, three deaths pre- senting with symptoms compatible with HCPS were reported in Anzoátegui, alongside two unexplained deaths among phy- sicians in Barinas; these cases remain unconfirmed7. Hantavirus outbreaks in Argentina, Chile, and the M/V Hon- dius cruise ship in 2026 highlight the need to revise epide- miological perspectives and clinical approaches to acute un- differentiated febrile illness in Latin America. The cruise ship outbreak remains one of the most significant events invol- ving ANDV, the only known hantavirus capable of interhu- man transmission. The outbreak was officially declared over, with no active transmission detected8. This eco-epidemiological and clinical challenge requires the expansion of diagnostic algorithms. The primary danger of hantavirus lies in its chameleon-like presentation during the early stages. Following anthropogenic ecosystem disruption and subsequent reservoir exposure5, patients enter a prodro- mal phase that closely mimics common tropical infections or viral respiratory illnesses, such as COVID-19. During the first 3 to 5 days, symptoms manifest as an acute undifferentiated febrile syndrome characterized by sudden high fever (>39°C), severe myalgias (particularly involving the back and lower ex- tremities), headache, chills, diaphoresis, and gastrointestinal distress, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain1,2. Increased vascular permeability driven by endothelial dysfunction is the hallmark feature of HCPS, driven by ele- vated viral loads and dysregulated inflammatory mediators, such as tumor necrosis factor, interleukin-6, and interferon- gamma. During this critical window, hantavirus infection is frequently misdiagnosed as dengue, influenza, leptospirosis, or COVID-19. In the case of ANDV, the transition to full HCPS Figure 1. Global distribution of the most important hantaviruses. SNV (Sin Nombre virus). Hantavirus: From Seoul to the Andes — The Imperative Need to Include It in the Triage of Acute Febrile Syndrome 247 occurs abruptly within hours, triggering a cytokine storm that leads to massive capillary leakage, non-cardiogenic pulmo- nary edema, and cardiogenic shock with high mortality ra- tes2,4. In most instances, establishing a diagnosis once frank respiratory failure develops is too late. This manuscript highlights an urgent priority for emergency triage: hantavirus must not remain a late diagnosis of exclu- sion but rather an active consideration in the systematic eva- luation of acute febrile syndromes and atypical pneumonias. Clinical suspicion should not be restricted to unexplained respiratory failure. We formally propose the integration of hantavirus into differential diagnostic protocols for patients reporting exposure to rural or wild environments within the preceding 4 weeks1. In countries such as Colombia, where endemic zones remain poorly defined, clinicians must rely on subtle early laboratory clues. The combination of thrombo- cytopenia, hemoconcentration, and circulating immunoblasts (atypical lymphocytes) on peripheral blood smears provides a cost-effective triad of suspicion prior to the appearance of bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiography1-5. When routine respiratory panels yield negative results in pa- tients with rapidly progressive pneumonia or in those pre- senting with febrile syndromes accompanied by early hema- tologic abnormalities, ordering IgM/IgG serology or RT-PCR for hantavirus should be protocolized9. IgM antibodies are detectable in nearly 100% of patients during the prodromal phase and persist for 2–3 months. Concurrently, IgG levels rise rapidly and appear to persist for years, although it re- mains uncertain whether these antibodies confer long-term neutralizing protection9. This rapid serological response at clinical onset makes ELISA the diagnostic tool of choice in emergency settings, outperforming RT-PCR in later stages, as the viral load declines rapidly after the first week of illness5. Furthermore, the unique capacity of ANDV for person-to- person transmission5 elevates early diagnosis from a clinical necessity to an urgent priority for hospital biosecurity and public health. Suspecting hantavirus infection at first contact in emergency departments is not an overreaction; it repre- sents the single opportunity to alter a potentially fatal course. In Colombia, the potential circulation of ANDV remains unk- nown, necessitating expanded seroprevalence and ecological reservoir research. Serologically, ANDV displays cross-reacti- vity with other New World hantaviruses, particularly SNV. We hypothesized that native Colombian hantaviruses may mani- fest with less aggressive clinical presentations than ANDV or SNV. This aligns with the findings of five patients diagnosed with IgM seroconversion in Córdoba and Meta10,11, presen- ting clinical features similar to those documented for Choclo virus in Panama12. To date, molecular detection in Colombia has been limited to a short genomic segment of the Neco- clí virus identified in wild rodents (Zygodontomys cherriei), although its human pathogenicity remains uncharacterized13. The geographic span of hantaviruses from North America to Patagonia underscores the fragility of ecological boundaries, which are dynamic interfaces that elevate global disease risk. Addressing this challenge requires a paradigm shift in clinical practices. Infectious disease and emergency medicine can no longer operate in isolation from environmental changes; the clinician’s diagnostic approach must be aligned with local te- rritorial ecology and epidemiology5,14. Systematically incorporating hantavirus into emergency tria- ge for acute febrile illness and atypical pneumonia is not an abstract taxonomical exercise but an essential clinical and public health imperative. In Colombia, substantial knowledge gaps remain regarding rodent-borne pathogens, particularly hantaviruses and Arenaviruses. Early clinical suspicion rema- ins the most effective tool in emergency medicine. Learning to recognize subtle epidemiological and hematological sig- nals in the early stages provides the only realistic window for intervention before fatal complications arise, a race against time in which early detection represents a major victory for preventive medicine. analysis.background: Hantaviruses comprise Old‑World Seoul virus (SV) transmitted by Rattus norvegicus causing hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (low lethality) and New‑World viruses such as Andes virus causing hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (30‑40% lethality); they share aerosol transmission routes and are often under‑diagnosed as other febrile illnesses.
analysis.methods: not reported in the supplied evidence
analysis.results: not reported in the supplied evidence
analysis.contribution: The editorial argues that hantavirus infection should be routinely considered in the triage of acute febrile syndrome to improve detection and clinical management, especially in regions where both Old‑World and New‑World strains circulate.

papers.title: Network-Guided Drug Repurposing for Hantaan Virus Infection in Endothelial Cells: Pathway Analysis, Target Identification, and Mechanistic ODE Simulations
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which are together the cause of more than 200,000 human cases every year. However, no specific antiviral therapy is approved. Here, we develop a three-stage computational framework for systematic drug repurposing. Transcriptome-wide analysis of hantavirus-infected human endothelial cells showed a response dominated by interferon pathways. A STRING protein–protein interaction network and a composite network centrality score identified 15 hub genes, including ISG15, IRF1, CXCL10, STAT1, and DDX58. Druggability and literature analysis of these hubs provided 12 repurposing candidates across four priority tiers. An ordinary differential equation (ODE) model of type I interferon signalling then evaluated eight drug perturbations. Early IFN-β achieved the fastest viral clearance (3.5 days) with reduced CXCL10 output. Early JAK inhibition delayed clearance (4.9 days) and increased IRF1-driven CXCL10. Our simulation showed that IFN-β combined with an anti-CXCL10 monoclonal antibody produced the best balance between antiviral effect and CXCL10 output. A structural sensitivity analysis showed the antiviral predictions to hold under an alternative network topology, while the chemokine predictions depended on it. This computational pipeline prioritises candidate therapies and phase-specific combinations for preclinical hantavirus studies.

papers.title_zh: 基于网络的药物再利用用于 汉滩病毒 感染的内皮细胞:通路分析、靶点识别与机制性 ODE 模拟

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒每年导致超过200,000例人类感染,且缺乏获批的抗病毒治疗。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者开发了一个三阶段计算框架,包括对感染的人类内皮细胞进行转录组分析,构建STRING蛋白-蛋白相互作用网络以识别15个枢纽基因,药物可及性筛选得到12个再利用候选药物,以及一个I型干扰素信号的ODE模型,用于评估八种药物扰动。
analysis_zh.results: 模拟表明,早期IFN-β实现最快的病毒清除(3.5天)并降低CXCL10产出;而早期JAK抑制延迟清除(4.9天)并增加IRF1驱动的CXCL10;IFN-β与抗CXCL10单克隆抗体的组合产生最佳的抗病毒‐趋化因子平衡,结构敏感性分析在不同网络拓扑下验证了抗病毒预测。

papers.title: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome: an emerging fatal zoonotic infection.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome is a potentially fatal respiratory zoonotic infection caused by New World hantaviruses, and it is acquired mostly via inhaling aerosolized excreta from infected rodents. Over the past 30 years, HCPS has expanded beyond its initial foci, and recent events suggest a potential for spread beyond traditionally endemic regions. The disease rapidly progresses from a vague prodrome to acute cardiopulmonary failure with a high fatality rate despite optimum supportive treatment. Pathophysiology involves endothelial failure, increased vascular permeability, acute thrombocytopenia and excessive immunological responses resulting in capillary leak syndrome and cardiogenic shock. It is still hard to clinically suspect early since the prodromal symptoms are vague and mirror common viral infections and respiratory disorders. Diagnostic confirmation needs serological testing or genetic approaches, which are typically unavailable in resource-limited endemic situations, leading to considerable diagnostic delays. Management is generally supportive, with early ICU admission, judicious hydration management, mechanical breathing and cardiopulmonary support including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in refractory patients. The recent multi-country Andes virus epidemic on a cruise ship in May 2026 highlights the potential for fast worldwide transmission of HCPS outside of usual endemic settings. This review summarizes the current information on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic techniques, and treatment options for HCPS. We also highlight the pressing need for improved global surveillance, rapid point-of-care diagnostics, global awareness among health care workers, and ongoing development of preventive vaccines and effective antiviral therapies to address this significant public health threat.

analysis_zh.background: HCPS 是一种潜在致命的呼吸道人畜共患感染,由新世界 汉坦病毒es 引起,主要通过吸入啮齿动物排泄物的气溶胶获得。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 该综述概述了内皮功能衰竭、血管通透性增加、血小板减少以及过度免疫反应是其核心病理生理,并涵盖了临床管理、诊断以及预防策略。
analysis_zh.current_state: 该疾病在最佳支持治疗下仍快速从模糊的前驱期进展至急性心肺衰竭,致死率极高。
analysis_zh.gaps: 早期临床怀疑较为困难,因为前驱症状缺乏特异性,且类似于常见的病毒或呼吸道疾病。
analysis_zh.future_research: 文中呼吁加强全球监测、快速现场诊断、疫苗研发以及有效的抗病毒治疗。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：HCPS 是一种潜在致命的呼吸道人畜共患感染,由新世界 汉坦病毒es 引起,主要通过吸入啮齿动物排泄物的气溶胶获得。 主要方向：该综述概述了内皮功能衰竭、血管通透性增加、血小板减少以及过度免疫反应是其核心病理生理,并涵盖了临床管理、诊断以及预防策略。 研究现状：该疾病在最佳支持治疗下仍快速从模糊的前驱期进展至急性心肺衰竭,致死率极高。 不足：早期临床怀疑较为困难,因为前驱症状缺乏特异性,且类似于常见的病毒或呼吸道疾病。 后续研究：文中呼吁加强全球监测、快速现场诊断、疫苗研发以及有效的抗病毒治疗。

papers.title: Hantavirus infection in Ukraine and the world: comparative analysis of the incidence dynamics of servicemen and civilians in peacetime and wartime
papers.abstract: Introduction. Every year, about 200 thousand cases of hantavirus infection are detected at the global level, a significant number of which have a course in the form of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Asia and Europe. The rapid course of the disease, the high mortality rate of its individual strains, which are mainly found in the Western Hemisphere, the lack of etiotropic pharmacotherapy and vaccination opportunities, as well as the characteristic features of the route of transmission of hantavirus disease (infection in the predominant most cases occurs as a result of contact with rodent body fluids), indicate that hantavirus infection remains a significant challenge to the health care system, which, nevertheless, is sporadic. Purpose. To highlight the quantitative indicators of the incidence of hantavirus infection in Ukraine among servicemen and civilians from 2014 until now in peacetime and wartime and compare them with the dynamics of incidence in specific countries and on different continents of the world. Materials and methods. In the course of forming the results of the study, the authors resorted to the bibliographic method, the method of information synthesis, comparison and generalization. The analysis of scientific literature on the subject of the work took place in the scientometric databases Scopus, PubMed, Google Scholar for the period from 2014 to the present. The value of the reliability of the approximation of the trend in the incidence of hantavirus infection among servicemen stationed in the Sumy region for the period from May to July 2025 inclusive was calculated, relative visualization was given without specifying absolute numbers, a graph of the specified trend was built, its line and equation were displayed. Results. During 2021-2026, it is worth noting the significant spatio-temporal diversity of hantavirus incidence, which is caused by the interrelated cumulative impact of the climatic features of a particular region, the transformation of ecosystems and the level of urbanization associated with the activities of the human species. In the context of the aggregate incidence of hantavirus disease among servicemen and civilians of Ukraine for the first quarter of 2026, it should be noted that a total of 63 cases of this disease were detected, which may indicate the continuation of a rapid trend and an exponential increase in the number of registered cases for the above-mentioned nosology in 2026 (as of March 2026). Conclusion. The analysis of the incidence of hantavirus infection in Ukraine from 2014 to 2026 indicates a unique epidemiological transition: from a long period of latent endemicity with sporadic case registration to a sudden epidemic outbreak in 2025-2026. In 2025, as a result of hostilities and the associated cascade of environmental factors, an increase in the incidence of this disease among the civilian population was registered in Ukraine, namely, 436 cases, of which 428 cases (which is 98.16% for the specified period) were detected in the Sumy region, which provoked an increase in the incidence among the servicemen of the Armed Forces of Ukraine stationed in the specified region, in particular, from May to July 2025 inclusive. The obtained trend of incidence dynamics for the specified period is highly reliable, since its value of the reliability of the approximation R2 is 0.8621 and this value is in the range from 0.8 to 1.0.

Materials and methods. In the course of forming the results of the study, the authors resorted to the bibliographic method, the method of information synthesis, comparison and generalization. The analysis of scientific literature on the subject of the work took place in the scientometric databases Scopus, PubMed, Google Scholar for the period from 2014 to the present. The value of the reliability of the approximation of the trend in the incidence of hantavirus infection among servicemen stationed in the Sumy region for the period from May to July 2025 inclusive was calculated, relative visualization was given without specifying absolute numbers, a graph of the specified trend was built, its line and equation were displayed. Results. During 2021-2026, it is worth noting the significant spatio-temporal diversity of hantavirus incidence, which is caused by the interrelated cumulative impact of the climatic features of a particular region, the transformation of ecosystems and the level of urbanization associated with the activities of the human species. In the context of the aggregate incidence of hantavirus disease among servicemen and civilians of Ukraine for the first quarter of 2026, it should be noted that a total of 63 cases of this disease were detected, which may indicate the continuation of a rapid trend and an exponential increase in the number of registered cases for the above-mentioned nosology in 2026 (as of March 2026). Conclusion. The analysis of the incidence of hantavirus infection in Ukraine from 2014 to 2026 indicates a unique epidemiological transition: from a long period of latent endemicity with sporadic case registration to a sudden epidemic outbreak in 2025-2026. In 2025, as a result of hostilities and the associated cascade of environmental factors, an increase in the incidence of this disease among the civilian population was registered in Ukraine, namely, 436 cases, of which 428 cases (which is 98.16% for the specified period) were detected in the Sumy region, which provoked an increase in the incidence among the servicemen of the Armed Forces of Ukraine stationed in the specified region, in particular, from May to July 2025 inclusive. The obtained trend of incidence dynamics for the specified period is highly reliable, since its value of the reliability of the approximation R2 is 0.8621 and this value is in the range from 0.8 to 1.0.

papers.full_text: 442 Infect Dis Clin Microbiol 2026; 8(5): 442–5 COMMENTARY Corresponding Author: Önder Ergönül E-mail: oergonul@ku.edu.tr Received: June 29, 2026 Accepted: August 7, 2026 Published: September 30, 2026 Suggested citation: Güllü D, Yigci D, Ergönül Ö. Is human-to-human transmission of Andes virus truly established? Lessons from the Hondius Cruise Ship experience. Infect Dis Clin Microbiol. 2026;8(5):442–5. DOI: 10.36519/idcm.2026.1246 Is Human-to-Human Transmission of Andes Virus Truly Established? Lessons from the Hondius Cruise Ship Experience This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License. Deniz Güllü1,2 , Defne Yigci1 , Önder Ergönül2,3 1 Koç University School of Medicine, İstanbul, Türkiye 2 Koç University İşBank Center for Infectious Diseases (KUISCID), İstanbul, Türkiye 3 Department of Infectious Diseases and Clinical Microbiology, Koç University School of Medicine, İstanbul, Türkiye TO THE EDITOR, T he recent cluster of Andes virus (ANDV) infection associated with the MV Hon- dius adventure cruise ship has sparked global concern about the virus's pan- demic potential (1). Cruise ships may provide favorable conditions for examining human-to-human transmission due to prolonged close contact. We reviewed the exist- ing literature to shed light on the subject. Most hantaviruses are considered strictly zoonotic pathogens. The primary route of trans- mission is through the inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta or contaminated environ- mental particles. However, reports from South America have suggested that ANDV may occasionally spread between humans under specific conditions. Initial reports emerged from family clusters in southern Argentina and Chile during the 1990s (2–4) (Figure 1). Investigators identified infections occurring after prolonged close exposure to symptom- atic patients (3). In later years, epidemiologic and molecular studies described additional clusters involving household members, sexual partners, and healthcare workers (5,6). A prospective study from Chile suggested that sexual partners and close household con- tacts had substantially higher infection risk than non-intimate contacts (7). Human-to-Human Transmission of Andes Virus Güllü D et al. 443 The strongest evidence of human-to-human trans- mission came from the 2018–2019 Epuyén out- break in Argentina. Martínez et al. (8) described 34 confirmed cases and proposed a “super-spreading” event during crowded gatherings. Using epidemi- ological reconstruction and genomic sequencing methods, researchers suggested that secondary transmission chains occurred following a single spillover. The authors estimated a median repro- ductive number of 2.12 before implementation of isolation and quarantine measures, decreasing to 0.96 afterward (8). However, reproduction numbers obtained from relatively small and highly clustered outbreaks are sensitive to assumptions about transmission chains, timing of exposure, and case attribution. During the Epuyén outbreak, transmis- sion appeared disproportionately associated with a limited number of individuals classified as “super- spreaders”. This suggests that social behavior and exposure intensity may have contributed to out- break dynamics. Accordingly, the estimated repro- ductive number may reflect the characteristics of the outbreak rather than the intrinsic transmis- sibility of ANDV itself. It is uncertain whether the reproduction number would be informative in the recent cruise ship-associated cluster. Furthermore, Figure 1. Infect Dis Clin Microbiol 2026; 8(5): 442–5 This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License. 444 such a high reproduction number has not been reported in other ANDV outbreaks. According to the authors, the human-to-human transmission win- dow of the virus was approximately one day, which may limit opportunities for transmission. Despite the available evidence suggesting potential human-to-human transmission, important epide- miologic and methodological limitations remain. In endemic rural areas, particularly among socially connected individuals living in close geographical proximity, shared environmental rodent exposure cannot always be ruled out. Recall bias, incomplete contact histories, and uncertainty regarding the pre- cise timing of infectivity challenge retrospective out- break analyses. The long incubation period of ANDV, which can extend up to 8 weeks, complicates the accurate reconstruction of exposure timelines and transmission chains. Genomic similarity between isolates may support an epidemiological link, but it does not independently prove direct human-to-hu- man transmission, since closely related viral strains can circulate within the same endemic region. Broader epidemiologic evidence also remains inconsistent. A systematic review by Toledo et al. (9) concluded that comparative studies did not provide strong evidence supporting widespread human- to-human transmission of hantaviruses, although limited transmission could not be excluded. Several seroepidemiologic studies evaluating healthcare workers and exposed household contacts similarly failed to demonstrate markedly increased seropos- itivity compared with the general population (2,7). In addition, no sustained community outbreaks resembling influenza-like respiratory spread have been documented despite decades of hantavirus surveillance in endemic regions. Therefore, the MV Hondius cluster offers a signifi- cant opportunity to re-evaluate these questions. Cruise ships represent theoretically favorable set- tings for transmission because of prolonged close contact, shared dining areas, confined social envi- ronments, and repeated interaction among passen- gers and crew members. The outbreak extended from symptom onset in the first probable case on April 2, 2026, to the last confirmed case on May 31, 2026, and was announced as over on July 2, 2026 (1). Since the incubation period of ANDV may extend to 8 weeks, this temporal pattern is com- patible with one or more transmission generations. Nonetheless, only 13 cases were identified among 147 passengers and crew members (1). The World Health Organization (WHO) initially estimated the effective reproduction number to be approximately 0.7 (10), consistent with limited transmission. Fol- lowing completion of the recommended 42-day follow-up, 317 high-risk and 336 low-risk contacts were monitored without identification of additional secondary cases. If ANDV consistently possessed highly efficient human-to-human transmissibility, broader dissemination might reasonably have been expected in such conditions. Instead, the restricted extent of spread may suggest that transmission requires highly specific epidemiologic circum- stances or intense close exposure rather than rou- tine casual interaction. Interpretation of the cruise-associated cluster remains complex. Some of the passengers report- edly participated in outdoor excursions and hiking activities in South America before symptom onset, introducing the possibility of rodent-associated environmental exposure before embarkation (11). Preliminary genomic analysis identified a single monophyletic viral lineage among cases from dif- ferent countries. This pattern is compatible with a common zoonotic introduction followed by sub- sequent spread (12). Together with the epidemio- logic investigation, these findings support limited human-to-human transmission aboard the vessel. Still, genomic data alone cannot resolve individual transmission chains or fully exclude alternative epidemiological scenarios. The outbreak additionally highlights important operational challenges relevant to future emerg- ing infections. The prolonged incubation period of ANDV complicates identification of index exposures and secondary cases. Rapid point-of- care diagnostic tests suitable for deployment in closed environments such as cruise ships remain unavailable. Moreover, current international sur- veillance systems are not optimized for rapid, coordinated investigation of uncommon zoonotic outbreaks involving multiple countries and mobile populations. analysis.methods: The authors performed a literature review of existing ANDV outbreak reports and epidemiologic studies.
analysis.results: They report that the 2018–2019 Epuyén outbreak had a median reproductive number of 2.12 before control measures, dropping to 0.96 afterward, and that transmission was concentrated among a few super‑spreaders; the authors note that such estimates may reflect outbreak characteristics rather than intrinsic transmissibility.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The authors examine the evidence for human-to-human transmission of Andes virus (ANDV), prompted by a recent cruise ship cluster and earlier South American family and household outbreaks. Methods: The authors performed a literature review of existing ANDV outbreak reports and epidemiologic studies. Results: They report that the 2018–2019 Epuyén outbreak had a median reproductive number of 2.12 before control measures, dropping to 0.96 afterward, and that transmission was concentrated among a few super‑spreaders; the authors note that such estimates may reflect outbreak characteristics rather than intrinsic transmissibility. Contribution: The commentary clarifies that while evidence suggests occasional human-to-human transmission, the data are limited and context‑dependent, highlighting the need for cautious interpretation. Limitations: Limitations include reliance on retrospective outbreak data, potential recall bias, incomplete contact histories, and uncertainty about infectivity timing.

papers.title: Multi-Country Human-to-Human Andes Virus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship: A Disaster Report on Prehospital, Health Care Facility, and Public Health System Challenges - Essential Knowledge for Frontline Clinicians.
papers.abstract: The Andes Virus (ANDV) outbreak reported on May 2, 2026, aboard a luxury vessel departing from Ushuaia, Patagonia, Argentina, was caused by an Orthohantavirus unique in its person-to-person transmissibility in contrast to zoonotic transmission characteristic of better-known hantaviruses. Containment required coordinated international management because passengers and crew embarked and disembarked at several international ports-of-call prior to outbreak recognition, resulting in cross-border transmission potential. Among those who disembarked, several traveled on flights to various destinations. Cases subsequently manifested in multiple countries, including Tristan da Cunha, Spain, France, Switzerland, South Africa, Canada, and The Netherlands. Upon notification, international health authorities implemented containment measures, such as contact tracing, quarantine, and isolation. Uniquely, ANDV poses distinctive risks due to its immediately prodromal presymptomatic transmission potential, initial non-specific flu-like symptoms, prolonged incubation period, conceivable long-term neurologic and endocrinologic sequalae, high case fatality rates (CFRs), and possibility of international dissemination. This report describes the successful management of a multi-national outbreak associated with cruise-ship travel, a setting with unique challenges. It also examines implications and challenges for prehospital, health care facility, and public health systems for future ANDV outbreaks. The event was characterized by delayed recognition, international spread, and complex coordination across multiple jurisdictions and sectors, including medical and public health authorities, policy- and decision-makers, crisis and emergency risk-communication experts, media, logistics, transportation, and security. Rapid implementation of public health measures coupled with clinician implementation of the Identify-Isolate-Inform (3I) model, a clinical framework to detect and prevent the spread of infectious disease, at the prehospital and health care facility levels are critical actions that can contain future ANDV outbreaks.

Event Description Event Type: Multi-Country Infectious Disease Outbreak Event Date: Index Case Boarded Ship on April 1, 2026; Outbreak Reported to the World Health Organization (WHO) on May 2, 2026; Concluded on July 2, 20261 Location: Luxury Cruise Ship MV Hondius Departing from Ushuaia, Patagonia, Argentina Response Type: Multi-National Medical and Public Health Introduction On May 2, 2026, the United Kingdom (UK) alerted the World Health Organization (WHO; Geneva, Switzerland) of an unprecedented multi-country outbreak of an Orthohantavirus on board the luxury cruise ship MV Hondius, a vessel that can accommodate approximately 250 people, consisting of passengers and crewmembers. The ship set sail on April 1, 2026 from Ushuaia, Patagonia, an area endemic for Orthohantavirus andesense, or Andes Virus (ANDV). Orthohantavirus are enveloped, negative-sense, single-stranded ribonucleic acid (RNA) viruses maintained primarily in rodent reservoirs; related hantaviruses have also been identified in bats and other small mammals. A significant number of individuals on the ship disembarked and traveled to various international destinations prior to awareness that they had been exposed to an infectious disease on board (Table 1). By the conclusion of the outbreak, there were a total of 13 cases (12 confirmed and one probable for ANDV). Overall, ten people recovered and three died, including https://www.cambridge.org/core/terms. https://doi.org/10.1017/S1049023X26109108 Downloaded from https://www.cambridge.org/core. IP address: 52.156.141.4, on 09 Oct 2026 at 02:21:16, subject to the Cambridge Core terms of use, available at the index case.2 Confirmed cases were managed in several coun- tries: South Africa, the Canary Islands, the Netherlands, Switzerland, France, Canada, and Tristan da Cunha (UK territory) (Figure 1).3 No rodents were aboard the ship,4 indicating person-to-person viral spread.5 While the situation is novel, the agent is not. Prospective data show that ANDV produces systemic viremia and shedding of infectious virus in oral and respiratory fluids.6 Outbreak genomic analyses support that this shedding can translate into limited person-to-person transmission in close- contact settings.5 There are no licensed antivirals or vaccines. Unlike other Orthohantavirus species (Table 2), ANDV creates enough viremia in human body fluids to allow for limited human- to-human transmission.7,8 Infected individuals who travel inter- nationally or remain in confined settings can drive chains of transmission that pose serious global health security and One Health concerns with potential for wide dissemination and major health and socioeconomic impacts. According to data from the vessel’s operator, Oceanwide Expeditions (Vlissingen, The Netherlands), least 33 passengers from 12 nations (Canada, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Singapore, Sweden, Switzerland, Türkiye, the UK, and the United States) disembarked the MV Hondius at St. Helena, a British island in the South Atlantic, between April 21-24.9 Other scientific publications cite slightly different numbers,10 highlighting the challenges with data collection and effective communication during a rapidly evolving outbreak. On April 25, most of those who left the ship traveled together on the only commercial flight out of St. Helena, landing in Johannesburg, South Africa later that day. From there, most continued onward to other world-wide destinations. United States residents returned to five different states (Arizona, California, Georgia, Texas, and Virginia), each with its own health authority. All these passengers traveled unmonitored while potentially infectious (Figure 1). While data are inconclusive, WHO endorses the working hypothesis that the index patient was infected before boarding the ship in Ushuaia on April 1, likely through zoonotic exposure to ANDV in Patagonia. A New England Journal of Medicine article published on May 20, 2026 reported he developed symptoms on approximately April 3.11 Given the typical incubation period of two to six weeks, this strongly supports the theory that infection was not acquired on the ship. His condition deteriorated rapidly, and he died onboard ten days after departure. His body was removed 13 days later in St. Helena. The second case, the wife of the index case, was a passenger on the flight from St. Helena to O.R. Tambo International Airport in Johannesburg, South Africa. She had symptoms prior to boarding,2 transferred to another flight bound for the Netherlands, but dis- embarked prior to takeoff. Subsequently, she collapsed at the Table 1. A flight attendant, who had not been on the ship, reported to hospital in the Netherlands with symptoms suggestive of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS; also known as hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, or HPS). While the flight attendant tested negative for ANDV on both polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and antibody tests, her symptoms raised concern for secondary transmission. This illustrates the importance of prehospital, health care facility, and public health system pre- paredness to rapidly identify and isolate potentially infectious patients until the cause of their symptoms can be determined. After the UK’s notification to WHO on May 2, the remaining passengers were restricted from leaving the ship and remained in their cabins. Between May 4-5, three symptomatic passengers were medically evacuated from the ship to the Netherlands. On May 6, as part of the organized disaster response, an emergency team boarded the MV Hondius. The team consisted of two public health experts from WHO and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC; Solna, Sweden) for situation assessment, and two Dutch medical experts for clinical assessment and management. After anchoring at Tenerife, Canary Islands, 85 passengers and 35 crew disembarked for immediate medical evacuation and repa- triation. Asymptomatic Spanish nationals were transported to a military facility in Madrid, Spain, and the others to their countries of origin. The WHO recommended that all remain in prolonged quarantine (42 days). The WHO asked countries with repatriated nationals to initiate precautionary contact tracing. Persons were categorized as high risk (placed in quarantine) or low risk (performed active self- monitoring) continuing for 42 days following last known exposure.12 Source The investigators obtained clinical and treatment data exclusively from publicly available sources, such as peer-reviewed literature and aggregate event descriptions. Limitations to this methodology are highlighted by the lack of comprehensive individual-level data, including contact-tracing details. Ethical Approval This report is based exclusively on publicly available information and aggregate event descriptions. The clinical and treatment data are from peer-reviewed literature. No individual-level data were used. This manuscript does not meet criteria for institutional review board evaluation. Observations Epidemiological Characteristics of Orthohantavirus In humans, pathogenic rodent-borne orthohantaviruses cause two major severe syndromes depending broadly on viral phylogeog- raphy: (1) hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), caused mainly by Eurasian species and characterized by capillary leak and acute kidney injury (AKI); and (2) HCPS, caused by American species and characterized by rapidly progressive noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, respiratory failure, and often, cardiogenic shock (Table 2 and Figure 2).7,13 The primary reservoir for ANDV is the long-tailed pygmy rice rat (Oligoryzomys longicaudatus).14 Spillovers to humans result from inhalation of aerosolized dried viral particles from con- taminated rodent urine, feces, or saliva.15 Andes Virus has a reproductive number (R0) of 2.12 – meaning, prior to outbreak containment measures, each infected person, on average, spreads the virus to more than two susceptible others, and so on, which can lead to an exponential rise in the epidemiologic curve.5 Effective public health measures can reduce the R0 to below 1.00, thereby halting the outbreak and preventing a global pandemic. Once there is an established outbreak of a hantavirus with cardiopulmonary syndrome, it is necessary for WHO Emergency Medical Teams,16 prehospital,17 and other health workers world- wide to have an available Identify-Isolate-Inform18,19 (3I) tool and Figure 1. Physicians and other health care professionals must be sufficiently knowledgeable to identify potential cases and reassure a frequently misinformed public when a different cause of symptoms is detected. Patients with ANDV have high viral loads in body fluids, which explains its unique ability among Orthohantavirus for documented person-to-person spread. Among Old World Orthohantavirus, Puumala Virus (PUUV) provides the clearest evidence of salivary shedding in humans; however, despite detectable viral RNA in saliva and salivary-gland tissue, epidemiologic evidence confirming person-to-person trans- mission is lacking.20,21 Scientific findings to date suggest that human-to-human transmission of ANDV requires close human contact, such as sharing utensils or food, deep kissing, sexual intimacy, and breastfeeding22 during the symptomatic prodromal phase.7 However, additional routes of transmission are plausible since ANDV can be aerosolized during severe coughing. analysis.background: The outbreak of Andes Virus (ANDV) reported on 2 May 2026 aboard a cruise ship departing from Ushuaia, Argentina, is notable because ANDV is an Orthohantavirus capable of person‑to‑person transmission, unlike most hantaviruses that are zoonotic.
analysis.methods: Containment required coordinated international management of passengers and crew who had disembarked at multiple ports (A2) and the implementation of public‑health measures such as notification, contact tracing, quarantine and isolation (A5).
analysis.results: Cases subsequently manifested in several countries, including Tristan da Cunha, Spain, France, Switzerland, South Africa, Canada and the Netherlands (A4).
analysis.contribution: The report describes successful multi‑national outbreak management (A7) and discusses implications for prehospital, health‑care facility and public‑health systems, emphasizing the Identify‑Isolate‑Inform (3I) clinical framework for future ANDV outbreaks (A8, A10).
analysis.limitations: Detailed epidemiologic data, case numbers, outcomes and quantitative case‑fatality rates are not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: Background: An Andes Virus outbreak on a cruise ship in May 2026 is notable for its rare human‑to‑human transmission. Methods: International coordination and public‑health actions (notification, contact tracing, quarantine, isolation) were employed. Results: Cases appeared in multiple countries (Tristan da Cunha, Spain, France, Switzerland, South Africa, Canada, Netherlands). Contribution: The report shows successful multi‑national management and highlights the Identify‑Isolate‑Inform model for prehospital and health‑care response. papers.title: Hantavirus in Dentistry: Occupational Exposure Considerations and a Proposed Tiered Infection Prevention and Control Framework-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective The aim of this study is to synthesize evidence on hantavirus transmission and occupational exposure pathways relevant to dentistry, and to propose an evidence‐informed tiered infection prevention and control (IPC) framework that distinguishes established from theoretical risk. Material and Methods The initial narrative search covered database inception through May 15, 2026 in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and WHO/CDC/ECDC/OSHA sources, followed by a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and public‐health guidance update through August 18, 2026. Approximately 1450 records were identified. After duplicate removal, 1070 records were subjected to title/abstract screening, 215 full‐text records were assessed for eligibility, and 45 sources were included in the final synthesis, comprising 34 peer‐reviewed publications and 11 gray‐literature or public‐health guidance sources. Results Environmental exposure to infected‐rodent contamination is the established occupational pathway. Limited person‐to‐person transmission is documented for the Andes virus (ANDV), but no dental transmission has been reported. ANDV RNA and culture‐based infectivity have been demonstrated in some oral/respiratory fluids; however, dental‐aerosol transmission has not been shown. Dental‐specific occupational risk therefore remains unquantified. Conclusions No dental transmission has been documented, and patient‐related risk remains uncertain. Standard precautions and rodent control are foundational; suspected or confirmed ANDV warrants transmission‐based precautions and airborne precautions for aerosol‐generating procedures according to current guidance. The proposed dental tiers are evidence‐informed, author‐derived, and unvalidated.

analysis.background: The review synthesizes evidence on hantavirus transmission and occupational exposure pathways relevant to dentistry and proposes an evidence‑informed tiered infection‑prevention framework (A1).
analysis.main_directions: It surveys literature through May‑August 2026 (A2) and examines environmental rodent exposure, limited person‑to‑person Andes virus transmission, and the distinction between established and theoretical dental risks (A5‑A8).
analysis.current_state: Environmental rodent contamination is the confirmed occupational route; Andes virus RNA and infectivity have been found in oral/respiratory fluids but dental‑aerosol transmission has not been documented, and no dental cases are reported (A5‑A8, A10).
analysis.gaps: Dental‑specific risk remains unquantified, the proposed tiered IPC framework is author‑derived and unvalidated, and patient‑related risk uncertainty persists (A9, A13, A10).
analysis.future_research: Validation of the tiered IPC model, quantitative risk assessment for dental aerosol procedures, surveillance for hantavirus in dental settings, and evaluation of rodent‑control and transmission‑based precautions are needed (A13).

analysis.summary_en: Background: The review synthesizes evidence on hantavirus transmission and occupational exposure in dentistry and proposes a tiered IPC framework (A1). Main directions: It surveys literature to May‑August 2026 (A2) and focuses on rodent exposure, limited Andes virus person‑to‑person spread, and distinguishing established versus theoretical dental risks (A5‑A8). Current state: Rodent contamination is the confirmed route; Andes virus can be present in oral fluids but dental aerosol transmission is undocumented and no dental cases exist (A5‑A8, A10). Gaps: Dental risk is unquantified, the tiered framework is unvalidated, and patient‑related risk remains uncertain (A9, A13, A10). Future research: Validate the IPC tiers, quantify aerosol risk, conduct surveillance in dental settings, and assess rodent‑control and transmission‑based precautions (A13).

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 在牙科:职业暴露考虑及提出的分层感染预防与控制框架——叙述性综述。

analysis_zh.background: 本综述综合了关于 汉坦病毒 传播及与牙科相关的职业暴露途径的证据,并提出了基于证据的分层感染预防框架 (A1)。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本研究检索了截至2026年5月至8月的文献 (A2),并审查了环境啮齿动物暴露、有限的人际 安第斯病毒 传播,以及已确立的牙科风险与理论风险的区别 (A5‐A8)。
analysis_zh.current_state: 环境啮齿动物污染是已确认的职业传播途径;在口腔/呼吸道液体中检测到 安第斯病毒 RNA 和感染性,但尚未记录牙科气溶胶传播,亦未报告牙科病例 (A5‐A8, A10)。
analysis_zh.gaps: 牙科特定风险仍未量化,所提出的分层 IPC 框架为作者自行制定且未验证,患者相关风险的不确定性仍然存在 (A9, A13, A10)。
analysis_zh.future_research: 需要对分层 IPC 模型进行验证,对牙科气溶胶操作进行定量风险评估,开展牙科环境中 汉坦病毒 的监测,并评估啮齿动物控制及基于传播的防护措施 (A13)。

papers.title: Open ecological, genomic and digital behavioural data resolve the 2026 MV Hondius Andes virus outbreak to the southern-Andean reservoir zone
papers.abstract: Abstract The 2026 Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulted in 11 confirmed cases and 3 deaths and raised questions regarding the origin of infection, with much media focus resting on a landfill in Tierra del Fuego. We evaluated competing exposure hypotheses by assembling open data on reservoir host occurrences, rodent serosurveys, and historical ANDV outbreaks along with the index case’s self-documented, publicly-posted citizen-science digital record of their movements. Historical outbreaks associated with human-to-human transmission were concentrated within a restricted region spanning southern Chile and adjacent western Argentina, coinciding with the distribution of the principal reservoir host, Oligoryzomys longicaudatus , and areas identified as elevated risk by multiple ecological and genetic models. The index case was documented within this transmission focus shortly before the putative exposure period. Together, our open data approach was able to rapidly locate initial exposure within the established ANDV transmission focus and develop scenarios to prioritise further epidemiological investigation.

papers.title_zh: 开放的生态、基因组和数字行为数据将2026年MV Hondius 安第斯病毒疫情定位至南安第斯储存区

analysis_zh.background: 2026年安第斯病毒在MV Hondius邮轮上的疫情导致11例确诊和3例死亡,促使对感染来源展开调查,媒体曾将其与火地岛的垃圾填埋场关联。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者通过整合储存宿主(Oligoryzomys longicaudatus)出现的开放数据、啮齿动物血清调查、历史安第斯病毒暴发以及首例病例公开发布的数字移动记录,比较了暴露假设。
analysis_zh.results: 历史上的人传人传播簇局限于智利南部和阿根廷西部,覆盖了储存宿主范围以及生态和遗传模型标记的高风险地区;首例病例在该传播焦点中被记录,时间紧邻推测的暴露期。
analysis_zh.contribution: 开放数据方法快速定位了已知安第斯病毒传播焦点内的可能暴露区,并生成情景以指导后续流行病学工作。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供摘要;详细方法、样本量以及定量验证均未在所提供的证据中报告。

papers.title: Hantavirus as a persistent zoonotic risk: epidemiology and current pharmacological management.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hantaviruses are emerging rodent-borne zoonotic viruses that continue to pose a public health concern despite their relatively low incidence in humans. The 2026 Andes virus outbreak linked to the MV Hondius cruise ship renewed international attention on these pathogens, highlighting unresolved questions regarding transmission dynamics, vulnerable populations, and global preparedness. This review provides an updated critical appraisal of recent advances in hantavirus epidemiology, emerging therapeutic strategies, and public health challenges, with particular emphasis on the 2026 Andes virus outbreak, companion animals, and solid organ transplant recipients. METHODS: A review of the recent literature was performed, focusing on zoonotic transmission, the role of companion animals, current and emerging therapeutic strategies, infections in immunocompromised and solid-organ transplant recipients, and the implications of the 2026 international outbreak. RESULTS: Although the sentinel hypothesis remains plausible, companion animals are not natural reservoirs, and preliminary evidence suggests that their exposure may reflect local hantavirus circulation, while pet rats have emerged as an important source of Seoul orthohantavirus infection. Therapeutic options remain limited: supportive care is the standard of treatment, and ribavirin shows benefit only in early hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. Emerging immunotherapeutic approaches, including neutralizing monoclonal antibodies and host-directed therapies, show promising preclinical results but still lack robust clinical validation. In immunocompromised patients, particularly solid-organ transplant recipients, hantavirus infection may mimic graft rejection or present with atypical, potentially fatal manifestations, posing diagnostic challenges. The 2026 MV Hondius outbreak reinforced the need for heightened surveillance, rapid diagnosis, and coordinated international response, while confirming that sustained human-to-human transmission remains exceptional. CONCLUSION: Recent evidence broadens the clinical and public health relevance of hantaviruses beyond their traditional framing as rodent-borne zoonoses. Advances in targeted therapeutics, integrated surveillance, and One Health preparedness will be pivotal to improving outbreak preparedness and accelerating the development of effective preventive and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Climate change, rodent ecology, and the rising risk of hantavirus outbreaks: an alarming public health concern.
papers.abstract: The Anthropocene era has been characterized by a higher risk of zoonotic viral outbreaks, which often result from a combination of factors, such as climate change, biodiversity loss, land-use patterns, and increased opportunities for human-animal interactions. The current perspective provides an integrated synthesis of how climate change-driven alterations in rodent ecology impact the molecular evolution, transmission dynamics, and emergence of hantaviruses, with an emphasis on the underlying virological mechanisms and their implications for One Health preparedness. Hantaviruses have undergone extensive diversification throughout their evolution and host adaptation and can infect rodents, bats, reptiles, and fish. Rodents serve as the principal natural reservoirs for hantaviruses, with many viral species exhibiting long-term evolutionary associations with specific rodent host species. Climate change has been recognized as one of the key determinants for the emergence of hantavirus outbreaks in different parts of the world. Climate-related factors may facilitate viral amplification through multiple mechanisms, including their impact on evolution, mutation, and reassortment. To conclude, climate change has shaped the ecology, transmission dynamics, and molecular evolution of hantaviruses by altering rodent behavior, their habitats, and the environmental persistence of viral particles. Climate-induced ecological disruption has created opportunities for viral amplification within reservoir hosts and augmented the risk of zoonotic spillover into humans. These insights provide a conceptual framework for anticipating future outbreaks in the context of climate change and support the integration of ecological, virological, and public health surveillance systems. There is an urgent need to ensure that virological preparedness strategies evolve in accordance with changing environmental conditions by strengthening genomic surveillance and integrated One Health frameworks.

papers.title_zh: 气候变化、啮齿动物生态与汉坦病毒暴发风险上升:令人警惕的公共卫生问题。

analysis_zh.background: 人类世时代因气候变化、生物多样性丧失、土地利用变化以及人畜接触增加,使人畜共患病毒暴发风险升高。(A1)
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本观点综合了气候驱动的啮齿动物生态变化如何影响汉坦病毒的分子进化、传播动力学和出现,强调病毒学机制及“一体健康”防备。(A2)
analysis_zh.current_state: 气候变化被视为全球汉坦病毒出现的关键驱动因素。(A5)
analysis_zh.gaps: 迫切需要根据不断变化的环境条件,调整病毒学防备措施,包括基因组监测和综合“一体健康”框架。(A10)
analysis_zh.future_research: 提出概念框架,以预测气候变化下的未来暴发,并整合生态、病毒学和公共卫生监测系统。(A9)

papers.title: Temporal epidemiology and multi-source forecasting of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and leptospirosis in mainland China: An interpretable machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Objective Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and leptospirosis are environmentally associated zoonoses in China, yet their long-term temporal dynamics and predictive determinants have not been systematically compared. Methods We analyzed monthly surveillance data on reported cases of HFRS and leptospirosis in mainland China from January 2010 to December 2025 using a multi-source data-driven framework. Five statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning models were evaluated using historical, socioeconomic, meteorological, ecological, and behavioral predictors. Results During the study period, 152,183 HFRS cases and 6288 leptospirosis cases were reported. HFRS declined significantly after 2019, whereas leptospirosis declined until 2018 and subsequently rebounded. Both diseases exhibited distinct seasonality, with HFRS peaking in late autumn and winter and leptospirosis in late summer and autumn. Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) with the combined predictor set achieved the best out-of-sample performance for both diseases. Shapley additive explanations identified 12-month-lagged incidence as the dominant predictor for both diseases, whereas precipitation and relative humidity contributed more strongly to leptospirosis than to HFRS. Conclusions HFRS and leptospirosis showed distinct epidemiological patterns and predictor contributions. Integrating multi-source predictors improved forecasting performance, while interpretable machine learning provided disease-specific insights to support early warning and targeted prevention of environmentally associated zoonoses.

analysis.summary_en: Background: HFRS and leptospirosis are environmentally linked zoonoses in China lacking systematic comparison of long‑term dynamics. Methods: Monthly case data (2010‑2025) were analyzed with a multi‑source framework, testing five statistical, ML, and deep‑learning models using diverse predictors. Results: 152,183 HFRS and 6,288 leptospirosis cases were reported; HFRS declined after 2019, leptospirosis declined until 2018 then rebounded; distinct seasonal peaks were observed; XGBoost performed best; 12‑month‑lagged incidence was the top predictor, with precipitation/humidity more important for leptospirosis. Limitations: Not reported in the supplied evidence; abstract only, limiting detail on methods and validation.

papers.title_zh: 中国大陆[ PDI0000 ]和钩端螺旋体病的时间流行病学及多源预测:可解释机器学习研究

analysis_zh.background: 肾综合征出血热和钩端螺旋体病是中国的环境相关人畜共患病,且其长期时间动态及预测决定因素尚未系统比较。
analysis_zh.methods: 对中国大陆2010年1月至2025年12月的月度报告病例监测数据采用多源数据驱动框架进行分析;评估了五种统计、机器学习和深度学习模型,使用历史、社会经济、气象、生态和行为预测因子。
analysis_zh.results: 报告病例152,183例肾综合征出血热和6,288例钩端螺旋体病;肾综合征出血热在2019年后显著下降,而钩端螺旋体病下降至2018年后出现反弹;肾综合征出血热在深秋/冬季达到峰值,钩端螺旋体病在晚夏/秋季达到峰值;XGBoost结合所有预测因子实现了最佳的样本外性能;SHAP分析表明,12个月滞后发病率是最主要的预测因子,降水量和相对湿度对钩端螺旋体病的贡献大于对肾综合征出血热的贡献。
analysis_zh.contribution: 研究显示两种疾病具有不同的流行病学模式和预测因子贡献,并证明将多源预测因子与可解释机器学习相结合可提升预测精度,支持环境相关人畜共患病的早期预警和精准防控。
analysis_zh.limitations: 在提供的证据中未报告;仅有摘要,缺乏数据质量、验证程序及外部可推广性等细节。

papers.title: [Nucleoside analogues in etiotropic therapy of hantavirus fevers].
papers.abstract: Hantavirus fevers (HF) are caused by pathogenic orthohantaviruses and are classified into two clinical forms: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), reported in Eurasia, and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), reported in the Americas. HF are characterised by an acute course with predominant involvement of internal organs: HFRS is mainly associated with kidney damage, while HPS is characterised by severe lung injury. Both diseases may also affect the central nervous and endocrine systems. In addition, hantavirus fevers are marked by severe complications during the acute phase and a prolonged recovery period. Currently, there is neither a WHO-approved vaccine nor any effective etiotropic anti-hantavirus therapy. The development of antiviral treatment strategies focuses on preventing orthohantavirus entry into cells or suppressing their intracellular replication. One of the main directions in the search for effective anti-hantavirus therapy is the low-molecular-weight compounds development and testing, many of which have demonstrated pronounced antiviral activity against orthohantaviruses through direct or indirect effects on viral RNA polymerase function. The review shows that new antiviral nucleoside compounds development and study has promising potential, as well as their combined use for effective etiotropic, pathogenetic and symptomatic treatment of hantavirus fevers.

analysis.main_directions: Antiviral strategies aim to block viral entry or suppress replication, focusing on low‑molecular‑weight compounds that target the viral RNA polymerase, especially nucleoside analogues, alone or in combination (A6, A7, A8).
analysis.current_state: HF shows acute organ involvement—kidney injury in HFRS, lung injury in HPS, and possible CNS/endocrine effects—and severe acute complications with prolonged recovery, while nucleoside compounds have demonstrated pronounced in‑vitro antiviral activity (A2, A3, A7).
analysis.gaps: There is a lack of approved therapeutics and limited clinical evidence for nucleoside analogues, leaving uncertainties about efficacy, safety, and optimal combination regimens (A5).
analysis.future_research: Further work should prioritize pre‑clinical optimization and clinical trials of nucleoside analogues, evaluation of combination pathogenetic‑symptomatic regimens, and expanded surveillance of treatment outcomes (A6, A7, A8).

analysis.summary_en: Background: HF caused by orthohantaviruses lacks approved vaccines or etiotropic drugs (A1, A5). Main directions: antiviral efforts target entry or replication, especially nucleoside analogues affecting RNA polymerase (A6, A7, A8). Current state: HF presents acute kidney or lung injury, possible CNS/endocrine involvement, severe complications, and nucleoside compounds show promising in‑vitro activity (A2, A3, A7). Gaps: No approved therapy and scant clinical data on nucleoside efficacy and safety (A5). Future research: advance pre‑clinical and clinical testing of nucleoside analogues, assess combination therapies, and improve outcome surveillance (A6, A7, A8).

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒 发热 (HF) 由致病的 正汉坦病毒es 引起,在欧亚地区表现为肾综合征出血热(HFRS),在美洲表现为汉坦病毒肺综合征(HPS),但目前尚无世界卫生组织批准的疫苗或病因治疗 (A1, A5).
analysis_zh.main_directions: 抗病毒策略旨在阻断病毒进入或抑制复制,重点关注靶向病毒RNA聚合酶的低分子量化合物,尤其是核苷类似物,可单独使用或联合使用 (A6, A7, A8).
analysis_zh.current_state: HF表现为急性器官受累——在肾综合征出血热中出现肾损伤,在汉坦病毒肺综合征中出现肺损伤,并可能涉及中枢神经系统/内分泌系统——伴随严重的急性并发症和恢复时间延长;与此同时,核苷类化合物已显示出显著的体外抗病毒活性 (A2, A3, A7).
analysis_zh.gaps: 目前缺乏获批的治疗药物,且核苷类似物的临床证据有限,导致对其疗效、安全性以及最佳联合方案存在不确定性 (A5).
analysis_zh.future_research: 后续工作应优先进行核苷类似物的临床前优化和临床试验,评估病理‐症状联合方案,并扩大对治疗结果的监测 (A6, A7, A8).

papers.title: [Andes virus aboard the MV Hondius: Transnational public health challenges in ocean-going cruise travel].
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the cluster of Andes virus infections that occurred aboard the expedition vessel MV Hondius during a transatlantic crossing. Drawing on publicly available information released by the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, it examines the key characteristics of this event: probable exposure in a natural reservoir area in South America before embarkation, limited human-to-human transmission in a closed maritime environment, difficulties in early case recognition, and the complexity of international contact tracing. The analysis shows that the vessel itself was not the source of the virus, but rather a setting in which public health risks were amplified due to prolonged cohabitation, limited onboard medical resources, and the cross-border mobility of passengers. Finally, the article highlights the importance of stratified contact management, timely reporting, effective international cooperation, and clear risk communication to avoid both underestimation of the risk and unnecessary public panic.

papers.title_zh: [安第斯病毒] 在MV Hondius号船上:跨国海上邮轮旅行中的公共卫生挑战

analysis_zh.background: 本文考察了在跨大西洋邮轮期间,探险船MV Hondius号上发生的安第斯病毒感染聚集,凸显了跨国公共卫生挑战。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者使用世界卫生组织(WHO)、欧洲疾病预防控制中心(ECDC)和美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)的公开信息进行描述性分析,重点关注南美洲可能的登船前暴露、有限的人际传播、早期病例识别困难以及国际接触追踪的复杂性。
analysis_zh.results: 分析得出结论,船本身并非安第斯病毒的来源;相反,长期同居、有限的船上医疗能力以及跨境乘客流动放大了公共卫生风险。
analysis_zh.contribution: 文章强调需要分层接触管理、快速报告、强有力的国际合作以及清晰的风险沟通,以防止低估风险和公众恐慌。
analysis_zh.limitations: 本研究仅基于摘要和二手数据来源;未在所提供证据中报告原始流行病学数据、详细方法和定量结果。
